citation: Conley, Walter H. (copyright holder) and O. E. Stelzer (artist), with Caroline M. McIlvaine (historical adviser). A map of Chicago: incorporated as a town August 5, 1833. 1933.
author: Walter H. Conley and O. E. Stelzer
repository: Norman B. Leventhal Map & Education Center, Boston Public Library
locator: identifier 06_01_014768; 44 x 64 cm, scale approx. 1:5,450, oriented north to the right
note: A 1933 RECONSTRUCTION, not a period document — pictorial elevations of individual 1833 structures with modern street names. The single richest building-level inventory available, and useless as primary evidence. Conley spent about two years in libraries and archives; McIlvaine had thirty years earlier collected data directly from the last surviving pioneers. It nevertheless contradicts textual sources (its 'Old Kinzie Mansion, built 1832' conflicts with every documentary account). Never sole evidence; no geometry traced from it.
